d8s1.actual: Tax-Free Childcare exists as a real, selectable rail — no longer a front-end-only stub. Against the DEPLOYED API with a real parent Firebase ID token: GET /api/my/tfc/config → 200 {"configured":false}; POST /api/my/tfc/link/start → 200 {"configured":false} (server/src/routes/tfc.ts + lib/tfc.ts are a full HMRC Tax-Free Childcare Payments API v1.2 client: /config, /link/start, /link/status, /balance, /pay, plus the public /api/tfc/callback). A provider can list it (settings.payMethods including "Tax-Free Childcare"), checkout maps it to the 'tfc' rail and renders the TFC panel, and POST /api/my/bookings {method:"Tax-Free Childcare"} → 201 with the method stored and pay Unpaid. So steps 2–10 are testable as a product rather than as a specification.
d8s1.notes: The rail is selectable but it is a PROMISE-TO-PAY rail today: with no HMRC credentials every route answers configured:false and the browser falls back to the reference the parent types in (features/listings/tfc.ts is explicit about the two switches, and NEXT_PUBLIC_HMRC_TFC is unset). d8s2.actual: The PROVIDER half is fixed; the REFERENCE half still fails the step's explicit check. Provider half: PUT /api/library settings.childcare is validated on write — {settingName:12345} → 400 'settings.childcare.settingName must be text'; a 60-char registrationNumber → 400 '…is too long (max 40 characters)'; a good write normalises ('EY 123 456' → 'EY123456', 'sw1a1aa' → 'SW1A 1AA', schemes ['Edenred','edenred','Computershare'] de-duped to two) — and it is published in the PUBLIC slice: GET /api/public/library/:tenantId → 200 with settings.childcare {settingName, registrationNumber, postcode, schemes}, so the 'add this provider to your HMRC account' panel renders for a signed-out booker. Reference half: it is still free text the parent types — items[].paymentRef, z.string().trim().max(120) (server/src/routes/my.ts:88). The spec's own bad example was accepted verbatim: a live booking (APF-10312, £80, Tax-Free Childcare, pay Unpaid) stored paymentRef 'Caelan'. The SAME reference 'ZAHERB78808TFC' was accepted on a second booking for a DIFFERENT child (201, APF-10314) — no uniqueness check per child or per booking, and nothing server-side mints one. There is format advice only: looksLikeTfcRef (/^[A-Za-z]{4}\d{5}TFC$/) drives referenceProblem 'malformed' on the ledger and referenceLooksValid on the childcare rows (verified both ways: 'ZAHE78808TFC' → referenceLooksValid true, referenceProblem null; 'Caelan' and a 6-letter prefix → malformed), but a malformed reference still creates the booking.
d8s2.notes: Judged on what the step asks: 'Check the reference is unique per child and per booking — not free text you type yourself.' Today it is free text, reusable across children and bookings. A system-issued per-child reference can only come from HMRC (routes/tfc.ts linkAccount), which is unconfigured — so this is a fail the HMRC integration would fix, not a coding slip. What HAS landed since the last verdict: the account details the step's first half asks for are now real and reach an unauthenticated booker.
d8s2.evidence: POST /api/my/bookings paymentRef 'Caelan' → 201 APF-10312; same ref on two bookings → 201; GET /api/public/library/:tenantId → settings.childcare; scratchpad/za-stripe-retest/za_part3.out.json (settings, d8s2) + za_part4.out.json (refFormat)

d8s7.actual: The inbound half still cannot be tested (no HMRC/EPP feed — d8s4). d8s11.notes: Two of the three items from the 13 Sept fail are answered (a promise/'sent' axis now exists as unconfirmed + promisedAt; the figures are computed server-side over a real range). The remaining blockers are Kaz's side (the tick column + date-ranged view) and copy (items 2 and 3), not the backend. One semantic nit: in rollUp() a row that is bank-matched but has no money in adds to reconciled.count but 0 to reconciled.amount, so reconciled.amount + unreconciled.amount need not equal gross — consistent with the documented meaning ('matched money' vs 'outstanding on unmatched rows'), but easy to misread on a dashboard.

FAILURE with a genuine Stripe refusal (not the app's own 'not configured' message): £40 booking APF-10314's charge was refunded OUTSIDE ActivityOS first (re_3UJZMIB8TXN2Ekrq0CUJuwrB, 4000, succeeded — i.e. the step's 'already-refunded payment'), then refund-approve → 502 'The refund didn't go through: Charge ch_3UJZMIB8TXN2Ekrq05lrM2vm has already been refunded.. p2-p9.notes: Was blocked ('needs the live server + a real staff token'). Now a real, reproducible failure. Blast radius is limited: the SSE payload is only a collection NAME (no data), and every REST refetch the nudge would trigger is 401 — so a switched-off staff member learns 'something in listings changed' and nothing more, until they disconnect. But the connection is unbounded: events.ts checks users.disabled/deactivatedAt only at connect time (routes/events.ts:57-64) and the Firestore listeners are never re-authorised. Fix shape: re-check the user (or a revocation generation) on a timer / before each send and res.end() the stream. Also worth updating the step text to the ticket handshake.

PASS for what the step asserts — but a sibling defect turned up while testing it, and it is the exact failure mode the step was written to catch, one event type over: replaying invoice.payment_FAILED (same invoice object, type flipped, genuinely signed) left the subscription state correct (past_due, pastDueSince stamped once and UNCHANGED on the replay — markPastDue is idempotent) yet wrote a SECOND 'Your ActivityOS payment failed' notification: the tenant's notification count went 1 → 2. Stripe retries deliveries, and stripeWebhook.ts keeps no processed-event-id ledger, so an operator can be told twice (bell + email). Only the money-moving path is idempotent; the notifying paths are not. Worth a backlog item: record event.id and no-op on a repeat, or dedupe notifyBilling by key+window.
